Job Requisition ID # 














 


26WD101042 
 
 
 Autodesk is looking for a Software Engineer to help develop a new Electron and Chromium-based desktop platform for Autodesk web applications. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will build and maintain components of the Electron application, work with Chromium configuration and desktop operating-system integrations, troubleshoot application and runtime issues, and contribute to making the platform secure, reliable, and reusable. You will work alongside senior engineers while developing deeper expertise in Electron, Chromium, Node.js, Windows, and desktop platform engineering.

 Responsibilities 
 Electron application development - approximately 40%: Develop and maintain features in the Electron main process, preload layer, renderer integration, and supporting Node.js components
 Chromium runtime and platform integration - approximately 20%: Work with supported Chromium and Electron configuration, command-line options, and build settings to enable capabilities required by the desktop platform
 Windows and native integration - approximately 20%: Implement desktop capabilities such as application lifecycle behavior, operating-system integration, hardware and system-information access, application protocols, and other native functionality
 Reliability, security, and troubleshooting - approximately 20%: Investigate application crashes, runtime problems, memory issues, security concerns, installation problems, and interactions between the web application and desktop environment
 Implement well-defined features and technical tasks from design through testing and code review
 Develop secure communication between web content and privileged desktop functionality using well-defined application interfaces
 Write unit and integration tests for the components you develop and contribute to the team's automated quality practices
 Work with senior engineers to apply Electron security best practices, including process isolation, restricted native APIs, secure inter-process communication, and controlled navigation
 Contribute to integrations with identity, crash reporting, telemetry, software distribution, and other desktop platform services.
 Help evaluate and adopt new Electron and Chromium versions and resolve compatibility issues when they arise
 Use profiling, logging, Chromium developer tools, and operating-system diagnostic tools to investigate technical problems
 Participate in design discussions, code reviews, sprint planning, technical investigations, and team retrospectives
 Work collaboratively with quality, build/release, product, and other engineering teams to deliver production-ready functionality
 Document technical implementations and lessons learned so knowledge can be shared across the team
 
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
 1+ years of professional software engineering experience
 Experience developing software using JavaScript or TypeScript
 Familiarity with Node.js and modern web application technologies
 Understanding of software engineering fundamentals including source control, testing, debugging, and code review
 Ability to troubleshoot typical software problems using logs, debuggers, and development tools
 Ability to learn unfamiliar technologies and apply guidance from more experienced engineers
 Strong collaboration and communication skills
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with Electron or another desktop application framework
 Familiarity with Chromium architecture, configuration, or developer tooling
 Experience developing Windows desktop software
 Experience with native Node.js modules or interoperability between JavaScript and native operating-system APIs
 Familiarity with C++ or another systems programming language
 Experience with Windows APIs, processes, registry, application lifecycle, or desktop security concepts
 Familiarity with desktop application packaging, installers, and code signing
 Experience diagnosing performance, memory, or application-startup problems
 Familiarity with continuous integration and automated software delivery
 
 The Ideal Candidate 
 You are curious about how software works below the web application layer and want to develop deeper expertise in desktop and runtime engineering.
 You enjoy debugging problems, learning new systems, and understanding how technologies such as Electron, Chromium, Node.js, and Windows interact. You can independently complete well-defined engineering tasks, ask for help when a problem moves beyond your experience, and use feedback from senior engineers to improve your solutions.
 You value clean code, automated testing, secure engineering practices, and collaborative problem solving.


 We are building a new desktop platform that enables Autodesk's web-based products to deliver richer, higher-performance experiences on Windows. Forma is the first product adopting the platform, with the longer-term goal of creating reusable desktop capabilities for additional Autodesk products.
 You will join a new cross-functional platform team working across Electron, Chromium, Windows desktop integration, software delivery, security, and enterprise deployment. You will collaborate with experienced engineers in Sheffield and with engineering teams across Autodesk.
 This is a hybrid working position based out of Autodesk's Sheffield office.

 About Autodesk
